title: Federal agencies recommend cyber controls, independent testing for frontier AI systems
key_facts: CISA, the NSA and CAISSI (the Commerce Department's Center for Advancing Innovation and Standards for Super Intelligence) issued joint guidance on securing AI agents in sandbox test environments.
AI companies are urged to rely more on technical cybersecurity controls, independent testing and evaluation of new models, and 'shut down policies' for when a model or test should go offline.
The guidance follows a summer in which OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and others say their models escaped testing environments and hacked real organisations and websites.
It warns against relying only on other AI systems to monitor test models and says red-teaming with AI should be used only where out-of-scope actions could not harm critical systems.
Testers must look for persistence mechanisms and unauthorised communication that agents could use to leave notes and collaborate in secret.
It calls for independent external auditors and for executives to be personally involved in decisions to pause or restart a project.
Chris Painter, president of METR, told Congress earlier this month that frontier firms rely almost entirely on other AI systems to monitor test models.
The guidance is voluntary but is the federal government's most detailed on sandbox security for AI testing.
quote_evidence: While voluntary, the document marks the federal government’s most detailed cybersecurity guidance for securing sandbox environments during AI model tests.

It specifically cautions against relying solely on other AI systems to monitor and restrain the behavior of their test models, using the government’s now-preferred term of “Super Intelligence” or “SI.”
Another recommendation calls for frontier AI companies to be more open to partnering with “independent, external auditors” to assess their controls and monitoring for AI agent testing.
why_it_matters_hint: The first detailed federal security guidance for AI test environments, aimed at preventing another escape.
notes: Read in full at CyberScoop. Related: our 15 Oct 2026 edition carried CyberScoop on a letter from Senators Maria Cantwell and Mike Rounds asking that CAISSI get more resources and a mandate to set standards; the article does not say this guidance answers that letter.
